content: A Mongolian spot, also known as a Mongolian blue spot, is a benign, flat, congenital birthmark characterized by wavy borders and an irregular shape. It is most commonly observed in individuals of East Asian descent, but it is also highly prevalent among East Africans and Native Americans. The name originates from its association with Mongolians. These spots typically fade away between three to five years of age and almost always disappear by puberty. The Mongolian spot is a congenital skin condition that arises during embryonic development. Its blue coloration is due to melanocytes, which are melanin-producing cells, being located deep within the dermis. These spots often appear as multiple smaller marks or a single large patch and are most commonly found on the lumbosacral region (lower back), buttocks, flanks, and shoulders. The condition occurs when melanocytes become trapped in the dermis during their migration from the neural crest to the epidermis. It is not influenced by the infant's sex, as both male and female newborns are equally likely to develop Mongolian spots. These marks are entirely harmless. However, for individuals unfamiliar with their origin, Mongolian spots may sometimes be mistaken for bruises. The prevalence of Mongolian spots is highest among Mongols and other East Asian populations, including Chinese, Koreans, Japanese, and Vietnamese. Nearly all East Asian infants (95-100%) are born with one or more Mongolian spots. The condition is also common when only one parent is of East Asian descent. Among East African infants, the prevalence is approximately 90-95%, while 85-90% of Native American infants are affected. In contrast, the incidence among Caucasians—defined here as the indigenous populations of Europe, the Middle East, North Africa, and the Indian subcontinent (including Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka)—is significantly lower, ranging from 1-10%. Among Hispanics, the prevalence is estimated to be 50-70%, likely due to the Native American genetic contribution in mestizos, who represent the largest racial group within the Hispanic population.
